children.why_this_cut: Introductory section: title and general statement about assistant guidelines; no cross-cutting linkage to later sections beyond the general concept of guidelines, which is seeded.

Sections with authority=user (Love humanity, Be rationally optimistic, Be responsible, Be interesting and interested, Be curious, Have conversational sense) plus Be clear and direct and Be suitably professional (authority=guideline). The only cross-link is the authority_level_ordering concept, seeded.

Remaining sections (Be warm, Don't make unprompted personal comments, Avoid being condescending, When appropriate be helpful when refusing, Use Markdown with LaTeX extensions, Be thorough but efficient) — all authority=guideline except Be warm which is also guideline; no cross-link to child 2 except authority_level_ordering.

expected_cross_links.evidence: Child 2's sections carry authority=user or authority=guideline tags; child 3's sections carry authority=guideline tags. The authority_level_ordering concept (root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority) is needed to interpret these tags, and is established outside this span (L69-101).
expected_cross_links.name: authority_level_ordering

expected_cross_links.evidence: Child 2's Be clear and direct section (L3756-3816) and Be suitably professional (L3818-3876) carry authority=guideline; child 3's sections also carry authority=guideline. Both children need the authority_level_ordering concept to interpret these tags.
expected_cross_links.name: authority_level_ordering

judgment_calls: Chose a 3-way split at L3505 and L3954 rather than a 2-way split at L3756, because the user-authority sections (L3506-3953) form a cohesive block of style guidelines with authority=user, while the guideline-authority sections (L3955-4251) form another block; a cut at L3756 would have split the user-authority block awkwardly.

The cut at L3954 places Be warm (authority=guideline) in child 3, even though it is stylistically similar to the user-authority sections in child 2; this is acceptable because the authority tag is the only cross-cutting linkage and it is seeded.

seed_vocabulary.name: authority_level_ordering
seed_vocabulary.prose: The ranking of instruction authority levels: root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority, used to determine which instruction prevails in conflicts.

seed_vocabulary.name: assistant_definition
seed_vocabulary.prose: The assistant is the entity the end user or developer interacts with; 'model' and 'assistant' are approximately synonymous in this document.

seed_vocabulary.name: conversation_definition
seed_vocabulary.prose: A conversation is a list of messages, each containing a role and content; roles determine authority of instructions.

seed_vocabulary.name: message_role_definition
seed_vocabulary.prose: The role of a message (system, developer, user, assistant, tool) specifies its source and determines authority in conflicts.

seed_vocabulary.name: chain_of_command_principle
seed_vocabulary.prose: The principle that instructions with higher authority override those with lower authority, designed to maximize steerability and control.
